en: to sink (of a ship); to go down under water

examples.en: A large ship sank in the sea.
The fishing boat almost sank because of the storm.

examples.ko: 영화 속 배는 빙산에 부딪혀 침몰해요.
examples.en: The ship in the movie hits an iceberg and sinks.

examples.ko: 배가 침몰하기 전에 승객들이 모두 내렸어요.
examples.en: All the passengers got off before the ship sank.

examples.ko: 침몰한 배를 찾는 작업이 계속되고 있어요.
examples.en: The work of searching for the sunken ship is continuing.

examples.ko: 오래전에 침몰하고 있던 배를 구한 이야기예요.
examples.en: It is a story about saving a ship that had been sinking long ago.

explain: 주로 배가 물에 가라앉는 사고에 써요. '가라앉다'보다 크고 심각한 사고 느낌이에요. 비유로 '회사가 침몰하다'처럼 크게 무너질 때도 써요.

phrases.en: They are looking for the sunken ship.
phrases.nuance_ko: 이미 가라앉은 배를 꾸밀 때 쓰는 관형형이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A modifier form for a ship that has already sunk.

phrases.en: I saw the news about the sinking accident.
phrases.nuance_ko: 뉴스에서 자주 듣는 짝말로, 배가 가라앉은 사고를 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: A common news phrase for an accident where a ship sank.

phrases.en: The ship seems about to sink.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-ㄹ 것 같다'와 함께 곧 일어날 일을 짐작해 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: With '-ㄹ 것 같다', it guesses something about to happen.

explain_en: A ship sinking under the water; news and accident reports. Mostly used when a ship goes under the water in an accident. It feels bigger and more serious than '가라앉다'. It is also used figuratively, as in '회사가 침몰하다', when something collapses badly.

t90.ax: A large ship sank in the sea.

examples.en: The bus goes around a curve up ahead.
The curve was sharp, so I drove slowly.
This road has a long curved section.
The pitcher fooled the batter with a curveball.
The bike slid on the curve.

examples.ko: 그 선수는 커브도 던질 줄 알아요.
examples.en: That player can throw a curveball too.

explain: 도로의 휘어진 곳에도, 야구에서 휘어서 날아가는 공에도 써요. 도로에서 심하게 굽은 곳은 '급커브'라고 불러요.

phrases.en: There's a sharp curve ahead, so be careful.
phrases.nuance_ko: 도로가 심하게 굽은 곳을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for a very sharp bend in the road.

phrases.en: I slow down on curvy roads.
phrases.nuance_ko: 휘어진 길 전체를 말할 때 '길'을 붙여요.
phrases.nuance_en: Add '길' to refer to a winding road as a whole.

phrases.en: The pitcher throws a good curveball.
phrases.nuance_ko: 야구에서 휘어서 날아가는 공을 던질 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used in baseball for throwing a ball that bends in the air.

explain_en: Loanword — road bends and baseball pitches (커브를 돌다) It is used for a bend in a road and for a pitch that bends in baseball. A very sharp bend in a road is called 급커브.

t90.ax: The bike slid on the curve.

examples.en: My bicycle tire went flat.
I was late for school because of a flat tire.

examples.ko: 타이어 펑크는 수리점에서 고칠 수 있어요.
examples.en: A tire puncture can be fixed at a repair shop.
I got a flat on the road and called my insurance company.
If you bail on an appointment, you lose trust.
The show fell through, so I got a refund.

explain: 타이어나 풍선에 구멍이 나서 바람이 빠지는 것이 기본 뜻이에요. 일상에서는 약속이나 일정이 갑자기 빠지거나 취소될 때도 '펑크 나다/내다'라고 말해요. 발음이 같은 음악 장르 '펑크'도 있으니 문맥으로 구별하세요.

phrases.en: to fall through; to have a gap
phrases.nuance_ko: 약속, 일정, 방송처럼 예정된 일이 갑자기 빠지거나 비는 것을 말해요. 돈이 모자랄 때도 '구멍이 났다'는 의미로 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when a planned appointment, schedule, or broadcast suddenly falls through or has a gap, and sometimes for a shortfall in money.

explain_en: The basic meaning is a hole in a tire or balloon that lets the air out. In daily life it is also used when an appointment or schedule suddenly falls through, as in '펑크 나다/내다'. There is also a same-sounding music genre (punk), so tell them apart by context.

examples.en: I got up before dawn and went to the airport.
Yesterday I couldn't fall asleep until the wee hours.

examples.ko: 꼭두새벽부터 공사 소리 때문에 잠이 깼어요.
examples.en: The construction noise woke me up before the crack of dawn.
How could you call at this hour? It's the middle of the night!
My father goes to the market before dawn.

examples.ko: 꼭두새벽에 출발했더니 길이 하나도 안 막혔어요.
examples.en: We left at the crack of dawn, so there was no traffic at all.

explain: '새벽'보다 훨씬 이른 시간이라는 점을 강조할 때 써요. 놀라거나 불평하는 말투에 자주 어울리고, 보통 '꼭두새벽에'로 말해요.

phrases.en: I got up before dawn and packed a lunch.
phrases.nuance_ko: 아주 이른 시간에 일어났다고 강조할 때 가장 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common way to stress that you got up very early.

phrases.en: Today there was construction noise from the crack of dawn.
phrases.nuance_ko: 그 시간에 시작된 일에 불평하거나 놀라는 느낌으로 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used with a complaining or surprised tone about something starting that early.

phrases.en: I left home in the wee hours for a business trip.
phrases.nuance_ko: 이른 시간에 어디로 떠날 때 '나가다, 나서다'와 함께 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Pairs with '나가다' or '나서다' when leaving somewhere very early.
phrases.en_equiv: to leave in the wee hours

explain_en: It emphasizes that the time is much earlier than ordinary '새벽'. It often goes with a surprised or complaining tone, and is usually said as '꼭두새벽에'.

en: to be delayed; to be postponed; to be pushed back

examples.en: The departure time was delayed because of the rain.

examples.ko: 회의가 다음 주로 늦춰질 것 같아요.
examples.en: The meeting seems likely to be pushed to next week.
I'm worried because the construction schedule keeps getting delayed.
I don't know why the announcement was suddenly delayed.
I wish the exam date would be pushed back.
I have so much work that lunchtime keeps getting later.

explain: '미뤄지다'와 거의 비슷하게 쓰고, 일정이나 출발 시간이 뒤로 가는 상황에 잘 맞아요. 반대말은 '앞당겨지다'예요.

phrases.en: The appointment was put off because I had a lot of work.
phrases.nuance_ko: '늦춰지다'와 거의 같은 뜻으로 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used almost the same as 늦춰지다.

phrases.en: The flight time seems like it will be delayed.
phrases.nuance_ko: 앞으로 늦어질 것 같다고 추측할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to guess that something will be delayed.
phrases.en_equiv: it seems it will be delayed

phrases.en: The test date was not postponed.
phrases.nuance_ko: 일정이 그대로일 때 부정형으로 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: The negative form says the schedule stayed the same.

explain_en: Passive, a set time or schedule gets moved later (시간이 늦춰지다) It is used much like '미뤄지다', and fits situations where a schedule or departure time moves later. The opposite is '앞당겨지다'.

t90.ax: I wish the exam date would be pushed back.

examples.en: During rush hour, the subway is packed with people.
I go to work early to avoid the rush hour.
I was late for the appointment because of the rush hour.
During the evening rush hour, it's even hard to catch a taxi.

examples.ko: 이 길은 러시아워에 차가 거의 안 움직여요.
examples.en: On this road, cars hardly move during rush hour.
Let's leave once the rush hour is over.

explain: 출근과 퇴근 때 사람과 차가 몰리는 시간이에요. 일상에서는 '출근 시간', '퇴근 시간'이라고 풀어서 많이 말해요. 영어 rush hour처럼 길이 막히는 시간이라는 느낌으로 써요.

phrases.en: If you take the bus during rush hour, it takes a long time.
phrases.nuance_ko: 조사 '에'를 붙여 그 시간대에 일어나는 일을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: With the particle 에 to say what happens at that time.

phrases.en: I avoided rush hour and went home early.
phrases.nuance_ko: 사람이 많은 시간을 피한다는 뜻으로 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often used to mean avoiding the crowded time.

phrases.en: Rush hour starts at six o'clock.
phrases.nuance_ko: 시간이 되면 사람이 몰리기 시작한다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means the crowds start to build up at that time.

explain_en: It is the time when people and cars crowd in around commuting. In daily talk people often say '출근 시간' or '퇴근 시간' instead. It is used just like English 'rush hour', for times when roads and trains are jammed.

examples.en: We usually get just one day off on January 1.
On the morning of January 1, I went to watch the sunrise.

examples.ko: 우리 가족은 신정보다 설날을 더 크게 보내요.
examples.en: My family celebrates the Lunar New Year more than January 1.
After January 1 passed, the weather got even colder.
New Year's Day is January 1 every year.
On New Year's Day I watched a movie with my friends.

explain: 신정은 양력 1월 1일이고, 설날은 음력 1월 1일이에요. 한국에서는 설날에 세배를 하고 떡국을 먹으며 가족이 모이는 큰 명절을 보내요. 신정은 하루만 쉬는 공휴일이라 상대적으로 조용해요.

phrases.en: The company closes for one day on New Year's Day.
phrases.nuance_ko: 조사 '에는'을 붙여 1월 1일에 하는 일이나 쉬는 일을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The particle '에는' is used to talk about what happens or whether people rest on January 1.

phrases.en: I ate tteokguk on New Year's morning.
phrases.nuance_ko: 그날 아침을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to refer to that morning.

phrases.en: Sinjeong is January 1st on the solar calendar.
phrases.nuance_ko: 신정의 날짜를 설명하는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A phrase that explains the date of Sinjeong.

explain_en: New Year on January 1, solar calendar. 신정 is January 1 on the solar calendar, while 설날 falls on the first day of the lunar calendar. On 설날 Koreans bow to their elders, eat 떡국 and gather as a family for a big holiday. 신정 is a one-day public holiday, so it is relatively quiet.

en: midnight; middle of the night; late night

examples.en: I suddenly wanted to eat ramyeon in the middle of the night.
I'm really sorry for calling so late at night.
My neighbors play loud music until late at night.

examples.ko: 야밤의 도시 풍경은 낮과 아주 달라요.
examples.en: The city scenery at midnight is very different from the daytime.
A cat visits the yard every night in the dead of night.
It's the middle of the night and the road is dark, so be careful.

explain: '한밤중'과 비슷하지만 '야밤에'는 '이런 시간에 왜?'라는 느낌이 섞일 때가 많아요. 그래서 갑자기 먹고 싶어지거나 전화가 오는 것처럼 뜻밖의 일과 잘 어울려요.

phrases.en: It rained in the middle of the night.
phrases.nuance_ko: 뜻이 비슷하지만 놀라움 없이 시간만 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: A similar word that just states the time without surprise.

phrases.en: Don't sneak out in the middle of the night.
phrases.nuance_ko: 조용히 몰래 하는 일과 잘 어울려요.
phrases.nuance_en: Fits well with things done quietly and secretly.

phrases.en: A phone call came suddenly in the middle of the night.
phrases.nuance_ko: 뜻밖의 일이 생겼을 때 잘 어울려요.
phrases.nuance_en: Fits well when something unexpected happens.

explain_en: It is similar to '한밤중' (the dead of night), but '야밤에' often carries a feeling of 'why at this hour?'. That is why it pairs well with unexpected things, like a sudden craving or a phone call.

t90.ax: I'm really sorry for calling so late at night.

examples.ko: 잠결에 전화를 받아서 무슨 말을 했는지 몰라요.
examples.en: I answered the phone half asleep, so I don't know what I said.

examples.ko: 어젯밤 일은 잠결이라 잘 기억나지 않아요.
examples.en: I was half asleep last night, so I don't remember it well.
The child recognizes Mom's voice even in their sleep.
My younger sibling got up half asleep and went to the bathroom.
It was just something said half asleep, so don't mind it.
It felt like a doze, and I couldn't tell if it was real or a dream.

explain: 거의 '잠결에' 형태로 써서, 잠이 덜 깬 상태에서 한 말이나 행동을 나타내요. '자다가'는 그냥 자는 도중이라는 뜻이고, '잠결에'는 정신이 흐릿했다는 느낌이 더 있어요.

phrases.en: I heard someone calling me in my sleep.
phrases.nuance_ko: 잠이 덜 깬 상태에서 들은 일을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes hearing something while half asleep.

phrases.example: 잠결에 한 말이니까 신경 쓰지 마세요.
phrases.en: I said it half asleep, so don't mind it.
phrases.nuance_ko: 잠이 덜 깬 채 한 말을 변명하거나 설명할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to excuse or explain something said half asleep.

phrases.en: I turned off the alarm half asleep and was late.
phrases.nuance_ko: 정신이 흐릿할 때 한 행동에 자주 붙여 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often attached to actions done in a daze.
phrases.en_equiv: to turn off the alarm half asleep

explain_en: It is almost always used as '잠결에' for something said or done while not fully awake. '자다가' just means 'while sleeping', but 잠결에 adds the feeling of being foggy and unaware.

examples.en: The newborn next door cries all night.

examples.ko: 갓난아이를 안을 때는 목을 받쳐 주세요.
examples.en: When you hold a newborn, support its neck.
Traveling with a newborn is not easy.
He fell fast asleep like a newborn baby.
They say breast milk is best for a newborn.

examples.ko: 우리 조카는 아직 갓난아이라서 하루 종일 자요.
examples.en: My nephew is still a newborn, so he sleeps all day.

explain: 태어난 지 얼마 안 된 아기를 말해요. 일상에서는 그냥 '아기'를 가장 많이 쓰고, '신생아'는 병원이나 뉴스처럼 격식 있는 자리에서 써요. '갓난애'는 줄여서 편하게 말할 때 나와요.

phrases.en: The newborn baby sleeps well.
phrases.nuance_ko: '갓난아이'를 줄인 말이라 편하게 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: A shortened form of 갓난아이 for casual talk.

phrases.en: I saw a newborn at the hospital.
phrases.nuance_ko: 병원이나 뉴스처럼 격식 있는 자리에서 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used in formal settings like hospitals and the news.

phrases.en: My aunt takes care of a newborn baby.
phrases.nuance_ko: 아기를 보살피는 일을 말할 때 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A common pairing for looking after a baby.
phrases.en_equiv: to take care of a newborn

explain_en: It refers to a baby who was born very recently. In daily life '아기' is most common, and '신생아' is used in formal settings such as hospitals or news. '갓난애' is the shortened, more casual form.

t90.ax: Traveling with a newborn is not easy.

examples.en: A thief broke into our house last night.

examples.ko: 경찰이 그 사람을 도둑놈으로 의심하고 있어요.
examples.en: The police suspect that man of being a thief.

examples.ko: 비싸게 팔다니, 가게 주인이 도둑놈 같아요.
examples.en: Selling it at that price, the shop owner is like a thief.
I had my wallet stolen by a thief at the market.

examples.ko: 영화에서 도둑놈과 경찰이 계속 서로 쫓고 쫓겨요.
examples.en: In the movie, the thief and the police keep chasing each other.
I heard the thieves broke the shop door and went in.

explain: '도둑'보다 거칠고, 화가 났거나 아주 친한 사이에서 쓰는 말이에요. 뉴스나 공식적인 자리에서는 '도둑'이나 '범인'이라고 해요. '놈'은 사람을 낮춰 부르는 말이라서 윗사람 앞에서는 쓰지 않아요.

phrases.en: a greedy, unfair attitude
phrases.nuance_ko: 남의 것을 거저 얻으려는 욕심 많은 마음을 비난할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to criticize a greedy wish to get something for nothing.

explain_en: A thief as a person, crude and derogatory, spoken. This is rougher than '도둑' and is used when you are angry or with close friends. In news or formal settings people say '도둑' or '범인'. '놈' is a word that looks down on a person, so do not use it in front of elders.

t90.ax: A thief broke into our house last night.

examples.en: The creditors came every day and knocked on the door.
He kept moving to avoid his creditors.

examples.ko: 빚쟁이한테 쫓기는 주인공이 나오는 드라마를 봤어요.
examples.en: I watched a drama with a main character chased by debt collectors.

examples.ko: 빚쟁이의 독촉이 대단해서 안 갚을 수가 없었어요.
examples.en: The creditor's demands were so intense that I couldn't help but repay.

examples.ko: 빚쟁이에게 시달리다 보니 잠도 못 잤어요.
examples.en: Being hounded by creditors, I couldn't even sleep.

examples.ko: 옛날 이야기에는 빚쟁이가 집까지 찾아오는 장면이 많아요.
examples.en: Old stories have many scenes where a creditor comes right to the house.

explain: 주로 돈을 받으려고 찾아오는 사람을 가리키는 말로 드라마나 이야기에 많이 나와요. 빚진 사람을 가리키기도 하고, 격식 있게는 '채권자'라고 해요.

phrases.en: I paid back all the money I borrowed to the creditor.
phrases.nuance_ko: '빚쟁이'보다 격식 있는 말이라 법이나 뉴스, 서류에서 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: A more formal word than 빚쟁이, used in law, news, and documents.

phrases.en: He was chased by his creditors and kept running away.
phrases.nuance_ko: 빚을 갚지 못해 돈 받으려는 사람을 피해 다니는 상황에 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when someone cannot repay a debt and is avoiding the people who want the money.

phrases.en: Every night a creditor came to the house.
phrases.nuance_ko: 돈을 받으러 직접 오는 장면에서 자주 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often said in scenes where someone comes in person to collect money.

explain_en: Colloquial, slightly negative, pesters the debtor. It mostly refers to a person who comes to collect money and appears often in dramas and stories. It can also refer to the person who owes the debt, and the formal word for a creditor is '채권자'.

en: to spread rumors; to gossip; to tell rumors

examples.en: Please don't spread this story to anyone.

examples.ko: 그 사람이 내 비밀을 온 동네에 소문냈어요.
examples.en: That person spread my secret all over the neighborhood.
Please spread the word to your friends that the shop is open.
It's a good restaurant, so I want to tell everyone about it.
It would be a problem if you spread this around.
I didn't mean to spread it around on purpose.

explain: 소문을 일부러 퍼뜨릴 때 써요. 나쁜 소문뿐 아니라 좋은 가게나 기쁜 소식을 널리 알릴 때도 쓸 수 있어요. 스스로 퍼지는 것은 '소문나다'(소문이 나다)를 써요.

phrases.example: 그 사람은 남의 얘기를 여기저기 소문내고 다녀요.
phrases.en: That person goes around spreading other people's stories.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-고 다니다'를 붙이면 여러 곳에 계속 퍼뜨리는 모습이 돼요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adding '-고 다니다' shows someone keeps spreading it around in many places.

phrases.en: Please don't spread my secret.
phrases.nuance_ko: 부탁할 때 쓰는 말투라서 '소문내지 마세요'보다 더 부드러워요.
phrases.nuance_en: A polite request form that sounds softer than '소문내지 마세요'.

phrases.en: I told my friends all about the new shop.
phrases.nuance_ko: 친한 사이에서 쓰는 반말이고, 좋은 소식을 알릴 때도 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Casual speech for close friends; it can also be used for spreading good news.

explain_en: It is used when someone deliberately spreads a rumor. It can be about bad gossip, but also about a good shop or happy news. When it spreads by itself, use '소문나다' (소문이 나다).

examples.ko: 다음 달에 가족들만 모여서 약혼식을 하기로 했어요.
examples.en: We decided to hold an engagement ceremony next month with just family.
Both sets of parents came to the engagement ceremony.
I had a hanbok made to wear on the engagement day.

examples.ko: 약혼식이 끝나고 다 같이 사진을 찍었어요.
examples.en: After the engagement ceremony, we all took a photo together.

examples.ko: 약혼식 없이 바로 결혼하는 커플도 있어요.
examples.en: Some couples marry right away without an engagement ceremony.

examples.ko: 약혼식에서 받은 반지를 아직도 끼고 있어요.
examples.en: I'm still wearing the ring I received at the engagement ceremony.

explain: '약혼'은 결혼을 약속하는 일이고, '약혼식'은 그것을 알리는 행사예요. 약혼식을 따로 하지 않고 양가 부모님이 처음 만나는 '상견례'만 하는 경우도 있어요.

phrases.en: We held an engagement ceremony at a small restaurant.
phrases.nuance_ko: 행사를 연다고 말할 때 쓰는 가장 기본 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The basic phrase for holding the event.

phrases.en: I attended my friend's engagement ceremony.
phrases.nuance_ko: 손님으로 갔을 때 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when you go as a guest.

phrases.en: We got engaged last year.
phrases.nuance_ko: 행사가 아니라 결혼을 약속하는 일 자체를 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers to the promise to marry itself, not the event.

explain_en: '약혼' is promising to marry, and '약혼식' is the event that marks it. Some couples skip a separate engagement ceremony and only hold a '상견례', the first meeting between the two families.
